title: SCR-002 stream resilience: reconnect resumes without gaps or duplicate rows
risk: A dropped telemetry stream leaves the console silently frozen, or reconnect replays the whole buffer so run rows duplicate and counters inflate.
preconditions: Namespace gov-scr-<case_id>-<worker_id>; the operator UI runs against the offline gateway and mock SSE/telemetry streams.
Operator session bound to tenant T1 and an explicit operator_id from fixtures/offline/governance.json; frozen clock 2026-01-15T10:00:00Z.
SSE stream subscribed at /api/v1/telemetry/stream with a resumable cursor; the window is frozen so ordering is deterministic.

steps.action: Subscribe and receive the first two run updates
steps.expected: Both rows appear, ordered by event time, and the client stores the latest cursor.

steps.action: Drop the connection and let two more events occur server-side
steps.expected: The console shows a disconnected/stale indicator rather than pretending to be live.
The two missed events (203, 204) are delivered and the console catches up; the connection indicator returns to live.

steps.action: Deliver one already-seen event again (replay of run-gov-202)
steps.expected: The duplicate is ignored by identity; the visible row count stays at four.

assertions: After reconnect the console contains exactly the four distinct runs once each: 201, 202, 203, 204.
The disconnected state was visible while the stream was down, so the operator never mistook stale data for live data.
Duplicate delivery does not create a second visible row and does not increment any counter.
Resumption uses the stored cursor rather than replaying from the beginning of the stream.
forbidden: Appending replayed events a second time.
Resetting the cursor on reconnect so either gaps or duplicates appear.
evidence: Event delivery log including the gap and the replay.
Cursor values before drop and after resume.
Visible row identity list proving four unique rows.
cleanup: Close the stream subscription and clear the gov- cursor and buffer keys.
automation: Command Center React components and the gateway routes run as real code under test; ERP, channel and telemetry providers are replaced by the offline mock sinks whose call logs are the oracle. UI assertions use accessible roles and names rather than CSS classes, and stream waits are condition-based. The drop and replay are scripted deterministically at the mock stream boundary; the client state machine is real code.
